title: Punnett Square Calculator + Dihybrid Cross Self-Test
description: Build a Punnett square for a monohybrid or dihybrid cross, get the gametes and both ratios, then check yourself on six questions with worked answers.
intro: Six questions on gametes, genotype and phenotype ratios and test crosses, each answer checkable against the square and the worked examples above.

questions.q: With independent assortment, how many distinct gamete types does an AaBb parent make?
options: Two, since there are two genes
Four, namely AB, Ab, aB, ab
Sixteen, the size of the grid
Three, as in the 3:1 ratio
questions.why: One allele is taken from each gene independently, so a double heterozygote gives 2 x 2 = 4 gamete types, which is why the dihybrid grid is 4 by 4.
questions.source: 'How a Punnett square works': 'A heterozygote for two genes (AaBb) makes four gametes: AB, Ab, aB, ab.' Arithmetic: 2 choices x 2 choices = 4, and 4 x 4 = the 16 boxes of worked example 1.

questions.q: Aa x Aa is crossed. What is the GENOTYPE ratio of the offspring?
options: 3 : 1, dominant over recessive
9 : 3 : 3 : 1 over four classes
1 : 2 : 1 for AA, Aa and aa
1 : 1, the test cross split
questions.why: The 3:1 figure is the phenotype ratio, because AA and Aa look alike, while the genotype ratio keeps them apart as 1:2:1.
questions.source: The four boxes of Aa x Aa are AA, Aa, Aa, aa, so genotypes are 1 : 2 : 1 and phenotypes group to 3 : 1. Page text: 'grouping boxes that show the same trait ... gives the phenotype ratio, which is where the classic 3:1 monohybrid ... ratios come from.'

questions.q: A plant showing the dominant trait is crossed with aa, and every offspring shows the dominant trait. What does that show?
options: It was Aa, since aa adds no dominant allele
The two genes must be linked, not assorting
Nothing, a test cross cannot separate them
It was AA, no recessive offspring appear
questions.why: Crossing with aa makes each offspring's phenotype report the unknown parent's gamete, so one recessive offspring would prove Aa and none at all points to AA.
questions.source: FAQ, 'What is a test cross and why does it matter?': 'All-dominant offspring means the unknown was AA; a roughly 1:1 split means it was Aa.' Worked example 2 shows the Aa case splitting 1 : 1.

questions.q: In AaBb x AaBb, what fraction of offspring show both recessive traits?
options: 1/16, the one aabb box of 16
3/16, one of the middle classes
1/4, from one half times one half
9/16, the both-dominant class
questions.why: Each gene independently gives the recessive pair in a quarter of offspring, so both at once is a quarter of a quarter.
questions.source: Worked example 1: 'aabb (both recessive) = 1/16', one box of the 16-box grid. Check by multiplying the single-gene odds: 1/4 x 1/4 = 1/16. The 1/4 option comes from using 1/2 x 1/2 instead.

questions.q: Which cross gives a 1:1:1:1 phenotype ratio?
options: AaBb x AaBb, both double heterozygotes
AaBb x aabb, a dihybrid test cross
Aa x Aa, a monohybrid between two Aa
AABb x Aabb, one parent homozygous
questions.why: A 1:1:1:1 ratio needs one parent whose gametes are all recessive, so the offspring simply read out the other parent's four gamete types.
questions.source: Practice problem 1: AaBb x aabb gives 'Grid (4x1): AaBb, Aabb, aaBb, aabb, each occurring exactly once', genotype and phenotype ratio 1 : 1 : 1 : 1. AaBb x AaBb gives 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 (example 1) and Aa x Aa gives 3 : 1. AABb x Aabb fills with AABb, AAbb, AaBb, Aabb, which is 2 A_B_ : 2 A_bb, a 1 : 1 phenotype ratio.

questions.q: Two genes sit close together on the same chromosome. Why does a plain Punnett square mislead?
options: The square assumes independent assortment
The square only works for one gene at a time
Dominance stops working when genes are close
You would need a 16-box grid instead of four
questions.why: A Punnett square treats every gamete combination as equally likely, which is only true when the genes assort independently.
questions.source: FAQ, 'Does this assume genes are on different chromosomes?': 'a standard Punnett square assumes independent assortment ... Genes physically close together are "linked" and need recombination frequency, not a simple Punnett square.'
